title: [WT-19] Integration and hardening: flip worktreeMode on, close parity, sweep file-only edges
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §7 (migration) and §8 (file-only dependency sweep). This is the epic's ONE integration-and-hardening task. The epic touched shared types (types/schema.ts: worktreeMode, workspaceMode, landingRetry), the MCP wire (claim/get_context workspace, finalize_attempt unlanded) and both wrappers, so full regression runs here.

Objective: turn worktree mode on by default only after the whole flow is proven end to end, and close the gaps no single slice could see.

Deliverable:
1. Flip the default in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.ts: `resolveWorktreeMode` returns 'on' when settings.worktreeMode is unset. Add vitest cases in validators.test.ts for unset→on, 'off'→off and 'on'→on. Change docs/CONFIGURATION.md's default to on, with the §7.4 rollback note ('off' restores shared mode).
2. Add the MOE_WORKTREE_, MOE_LAND_, MOE_CONTROL_ and MOE_BOARD_ families to the compared families in scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1.
3. File-only dependency sweep with moe.set_task_dependencies. Start from the governor audit list in §8: V07←01f37ac6, V04c←V08b, RF04←90664db1, RF07←465ee875, RF07←80930ce6, R13←R11e, R13←2cf1c6be, 724e31fa←e7f4026a, 01f37ac6←e7f4026a. For every still-open task's edge A←B, apply the §8 re-derivation rule: keep it if A names anything B produces; drop it only when the sole overlap is a shared existing file. The completion summary lists each edge as kept or dropped, with a reason.
4. Full regression (record pass counts):
   - npm test in packages/moe-daemon, packages/moe-proxy and packages/moe-claude-plugin;
   - bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and pwsh scripts/tests/postflight.ps1;
   - the worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} suites from WT-08T;
   - parity-check.{sh,ps1};
   - cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test, run under a jetbrains-gradle lease (moe.acquire_resource);
   - npm run lint.
5. End-to-end check in a throwaway repo made by `git init` under mktemp, with worktreeMode on. Two tasks in parallel touch disjoint files and both land on main. A third conflicts, goes to unlanded, then lands after the resume. Assert main's history is linear with no force-push (reflog shows only fast-forward updates).
6. Whole-epic adversarial pass (adversarial-self-review) over `git diff <epic base>..main` against the doc's §2-§6 contracts: drift between producer and consumer (daemon field names vs wrapper reads), sh/ps1 twin drift, codes documented in WT-17 but never emitted. Fix findings inside these files, or file them as bug: tasks in this epic.
7. Post the flip runbook (TROUBLESHOOTING section from WT-16) to #general for the human. Say that this project's worker seats stop with MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING until the control checkout is switched to moe/control.

NOT in scope: new features; re-editing docs other than CONFIGURATION.md (findings there become bug: tasks); changing shared-mode behavior.

Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/validators.test.ts && npm test && cd ../.. && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh && npm run lint
definitionOfDone: resolveWorktreeMode defaults to 'on' (validators.test.ts covers unset/on/off) and docs/CONFIGURATION.md states default on plus the 'off' rollback.
parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 compare the MOE_WORKTREE_, MOE_LAND_, MOE_CONTROL_ and MOE_BOARD_ families, and both exit 0.
Every audited dependsOn edge, and every open edge re-derived by the §8 rule, is kept or dropped via moe.set_task_dependencies, with the list and reasons in the completion summary.
Full regression is green with recorded counts: daemon/proxy/claude-plugin npm test, postflight.{sh,ps1}, worktree-landing.{sh,ps1}, ./gradlew test (under the jetbrains-gradle lease) and npm run lint.
The throwaway-repo end-to-end run lands two parallel tasks plus one conflict-resumed task on main with fast-forward-only history.
The whole-epic adversarial findings are fixed or filed as bug: tasks, and the flip runbook is posted to #general naming MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING.
taskRails: DoD readings for QA. DoD 3: the completion summary classifies every candidate edge as 'moot' (an end is DONE/ARCHIVED), 'kept (produces)' naming what B produces, or 'drop-after-runbook' (the only overlap is a shared existing file). Kept and moot edges need no moe.set_task_dependencies call. A drop-after-runbook edge counts as handled when the summary lists it with its reason and the step-5 #general post hands it to governors. A governor removes it only once this project runs in worktree mode, which is after this row's QA, so QA must not require those removals. DoD 1: 'defaults to on' means the (b) the human approved, in decision dec-eb7b8337 or a row comment of theirs. With the recommended (b), unset resolves to 'on' only with a non-blank qualityGate, else 'off'.

implementationPlan.description:
Close parity (DoD 2, plus item 1 of WT-S comment-54c4e7a6). Nothing here depends on the flip.

parity-check.sh:
- Append 'MOE_WORKTREE_' 'MOE_LAND_' 'MOE_CONTROL_' 'MOE_BOARD_' 'MOE_PUSH_' 'MOE_MIGRATION_' to the section-1 family loop. That loop already fails on an empty sh family or a difference between the twins.
- Add the single code MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE to section 2's require_both list.
- Do NOT add MOE_WRAPPER_ as a family. The sh wrapper carries sh-only internal MOE_WRAPPER_* names (at rev 1: ARGV, CURRENT_HASH, DEFERRED_HASH, LAUNCH_HASH, PARSE_ERR, PARSE_RC, PATH and REFUSED_HASH); re-grep at HEAD.

parity-check.ps1:
- Add the same six families to $dynamicPatterns. If any landed code carries a digit, make the pattern accept digits; grep both wrappers to check.
- Add MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE to $required.

Stale allowlist:
- Remove the INTERNAL_PLUMBING entries that neither wrapper contains any more. At rev 1 these were MOE_ATTR_UNDECLARED, MOE_ATTR_EXCLUDE, MOE_ATTR_POLICY_OVERRIDE and MOE_COMMIT_BOARD_STATE; re-check at HEAD.
- Keep the mechanism.
- Fix the ps1 NOTE comment's names: they are now MOE_PY_*, which is not a compared family.

A new-family token present in only one twin:
- An internal env-bridge name joins the allowlist in BOTH scripts, with a comment.
- An operator-visible code missing from one twin is an epic defect. If emitting it at the twin's equivalent site is a one-line wrapper edit, make it and report scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} in modifiedFiles. Otherwise file a bug: task in this epic and stop, because DoD 2 needs exit 0.

Error handling: both scripts keep failing on any asymmetry and on an empty family. Never allowlist a whole family.

Test: `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` and `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$(wslpath -w scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1)"` both exit 0.

Commit an end-to-end check of the whole flow (DoD 5) as a new file, scripts/tests/worktree-e2e.cjs. It does not depend on the flip: the scratch project sets worktreeMode 'on' explicitly.

Model it on WT-04T's scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs:
- the same CLI shape, `<sh|ps1> <wrapper> <fake-proxy> <parent-tmp> <engine>`;
- a `cli` fake-CLI mode;
- one result line per scenario, and exit 1 on any failure;
- no output line starting with SKIP.

Setup:
- The real wrappers with the shared fake daemon+proxy. Per WT-S comment-ce50a0ee, no real daemon is needed.
- One scratch repo from `git init` under mktemp, with branch main.
- The control checkout on moe/control.
- .moe/project.json settings {worktreeMode:'on', consolidationBranch:'main'}, gate-less like WT-08T's cases. Gated landings are WT-10's held-out cases; name them in the summary.

Scenarios:
(a) parallel. Launch two worker seats at once, with different worker ids and tasks (task-a, task-b). Each fake CLI writes its own file in its W (its cwd) and completes. Both must land:
- main gains exactly two commits;
- `git log --first-parent main` is linear;
- every `git reflog refs/heads/main` entry's new value descends from its old one (fast-forward only, never forced);
- neither W holds .moe.
(b) conflict-resume.
- task-c's fake CLI changes a line that task-a already landed differently.
- The landing ends unlanded on a conflict, main does not move, and the fake records finalize_attempt outcome 'unlanded'.
- A second session of task-c gets the LANDING-CONFLICT prompt (WT-11). Its fake CLI resolves the markers and completes, and the task lands.
- History stays linear and fast-forward only.
(c) WT-S comment-54c4e7a6 item 2:
- The remote race: A publishes while B's fetch and push fail. There must be no fork (local == origin), and B ends unlanded 'remote'.
- An unknown push outcome that receipt_replay later resolves.
- If WT-08T's or WT-09's worktree-landing suites already cover these, name those cases here and let step 6 run them. Add a case to this file only if one is missing.

Fake-proxy support:
- Reuse the knobs that WT-04T, WT-08T and WT-11 added: per-seat task ids, workspace, finalize 'unlanded', landingRetry.
- Add a missing knob to scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js only as an opt-in knob. With it unset, every answer stays byte-identical.
- Never edit a held-out suite.

Error handling: a scenario that can't be set up (git missing, a fixture command failing) fails with its reason; it never passes vacuously. Cleanup removes only the mktemp tree, on every exit path.

Test: `node scripts/tests/worktree-e2e.cjs sh scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js "$(mktemp -d)" "$(command -v bash)"` prints ok for (a) and (b), and for (c) when its cases live here. The ps1 engine leg runs in step 6.

HUMAN GATE. This is the one gate before any flip step; steps 1-2 flip nothing.

Before step 4, read this row's comments with `moe.get_context {taskId, commentsLimit: 50, commentsMaxChars: 0}`. You need the human's go on BOTH parts:
(a) the product-wide default flip of worktreeMode;
(b) the answer for projects without a qualityGate.

A go counts only if it comes from the human:
- their own row comment;
- or a decision or chat message of theirs that a governor's row comment cites by id.
Quote it in your step note.

What to do:
- The go approves the recommended (b) below: continue to step 4 as written.
- The go picks another (b): do not improvise. Call moe.request_replan quoting it, because the files change. For example, the stricter option adds a claimNextTask.ts refusal, a new code and its docs.
- No go is recorded:
  1. Post the ask below verbatim with moe.chat_decision {channel: 'chan-b6d8273b'}. If a governor already posted a pending decision with the same content, reuse it instead.
  2. Add a row comment naming the decision id.
  3. Call moe.report_blocked {needsFrom: 'human'} with a reason naming that id. This frees your seat, and a governor restores the row after the go.
  Never flip, edit validators.ts, or rebuild the live daemon or IDE plugin without the go. Builds inside isolated test snapshots are fine.

Recommended (b):
- An unset worktreeMode resolves to 'on' only when settings.qualityGate is a string that is non-blank after trim, which is the same test the wrappers' gate read uses. Otherwise it resolves to 'off'.
- Explicit 'on' and 'off' are honored as written.
- Explicit 'on' with no gate stays WT-16's doctor failure and a runbook precondition, not a runtime refusal. Design §2.2 rejected a wrapper refusal because the gate-less scratch cases of WT-08T and WT-10 land with explicit 'on'.

Ask (910 chars; the cap is 1000):
"WT-19 (task-b1ca54f2) needs your go on the worktree default, one decision in two parts:
(a) Flip: an unset settings.worktreeMode means worktree mode, product-wide, once the daemon or plugin is rebuilt with WT-19.
(b) Gate-less projects: unset resolves to 'on' only when settings.qualityGate is non-blank. Without a gate it stays 'off', so shared mode is unchanged. Explicit 'on'/'off' are honored; explicit 'on' with no gate stays a doctor failure. A stricter option also refuses a worktree claim with no gate.
Effect: a project with a qualityGate and no worktreeMode switches at its next worker claim. Its workers then stop with MOE_CONTROL_NOT_FOLLOWING until it runs the TROUBLESHOOTING 'Worktree mode' runbook. To opt out, set worktreeMode 'off'. This project has no qualityGate, so it switches only when you run the runbook.
Approve = go on (a)+(b). To choose another (b), reject and comment on the task."

Error handling: an ambiguous answer, or one that approves only (a) or only (b), is not a go. Ask again in the decision thread and stay blocked.

Flip the default with the approved (b) (DoD 1). Before editing, read WT-01's landed code and Serena decision-worktree-attempt-workspace-contract.

packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.ts, resolveWorktreeMode, the ONE place the default lives:
- Widen the parameter type to `{ worktreeMode?: unknown; qualityGate?: unknown } | null`.
- A defined key is validated exactly as today: 'on' and 'off' as written; every other value, null included, is INVALID_INPUT.
- An undefined key returns 'on' iff `typeof qualityGate === 'string' && qualityGate.trim() !== ''`, else 'off'. Never throw on an odd qualityGate type; that just means no gate.
- Update the doc comment with the rule and the reason: rail 1, landings only with a gate.

packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts: rewrite ProjectSettings.worktreeMode's comment ("Absent means 'off' only in resolveWorktreeMode (WT-19 flips that default)") to state the new rule. Comment only.

Tests (mutation-resistant, exact values):
- validators.test.ts covers DoD 1's unset/on/off rows:
  - unset + no gate → 'off'; unset + 'npm test' → 'on'; unset + '   ' → 'off'; unset + gate 7 → 'off';

Tests that encode the old default:

- A fixture that sets a non-blank qualityGate and omits worktreeMode now gets worktree mode for WORKING claims. Where that test's intent is shared mode, pin `worktreeMode: 'off'` in its settings fixture, and never change its assertions.

docs/CONFIGURATION.md, the worktreeMode row WT-17 wrote:
- The default is 'on' when a non-blank qualityGate is set, else 'off'.
- Add the §7.4 rollback note:
  - 'off' restores shared mode for NEW attempts; an open attempt keeps its pinned mode;

comments.author: architect-899a90d6
comments.content:
Two hardening items WT-03 (task-9a39bf6a) left out of its slice, for this task's adversarial pass:
1. The UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST in server/WebSocketServer.ts lacks 'landingRetry'. A stale full-task board echo could bring back a cleared landingRetry, which causes a spurious LANDING-RETRY or an early BLOCKED. A board client could also forge one.
2. nextStatusForRelease in state/workerLifecycle.ts routes a WORKING row whose steps are all COMPLETED to REVIEW. A landingRetry row keeps its steps COMPLETED, so releasing a dead worker during a conflict resume would hand QA a task with nothing landed. The row should stay WORKING while landingRetry is set.
Both are small. If WT-19 is over its file cap, split them into their own row.

comments.author: qa-952969be
comments.content:
@governor-693b7073 QA note from the WT-S round-2 review (qa-952969be), for this row's adversarial pass and the human's flip decision.

1. Gate-less projects after the flip.
- The design gates a worktree landing only while settings.qualityGate is set (§2.2 L3/L6).
- WT-16's doctor hard-fails worktreeMode 'on' without a gate, but nothing enforces that at runtime.
- Once this row makes unset resolve to 'on', every project without a qualityGate moves main ungated, and its doctor fails. Rail 1 says main moves only after the task's gate passes.
- Decide this with the human before flipping. For example: resolveWorktreeMode resolves unset to 'on' only when a qualityGate is set, or a worktree-mode claim or landing refuses without one.

2. Docs that the §7.6 sweep misses, owned by neither WT-17 nor WT-18:
- docs/skills/moe-epic-breakdown/SKILL.md:78 tells architects that same-file tasks are "a sequencing decision". That rule is what creates file-only edges, so epic goal 5 (architects stop chaining tasks that only share a file) needs it changed for worktree mode.
- The QA empty-ledger self-landing fallback (docs/roles/qa.md:15, qa.reference.md:42, docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md:26) lands from the shared working tree. In worktree mode that tree is the control checkout on moe/control. A QA self-landing would commit onto moe/control, which raises MOE_CONTROL_CHECKOUT_DIVERGED (§6) and contradicts §3.6/§3.7. A nothing-to-commit landing (§2.9) can reach this path.

File these as bug: tasks, or fold them into a docs row, per this row's DoD 6.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- resolveWorktreeMode(settings) is the only default. claimNextTask.ts:156 calls it with state.project?.settings, the whole object. WT-16's plan reads the mode through the WT-01 resolver.
- The wrappers never read worktreeMode: they take the mode from the claim's workspace, so flipping the default is a daemon-only change.
- The wrappers treat a qualityGate as set when it is non-blank after trim (sh python read, ps1 Trim()), and MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1 clears it per seat.
- The epic's finalTaskId is now pinned to WT-19.
- The live daemon is the IDE-bundled build, so a flip reaches projects only after a daemon or plugin rebuild.

- A gate added later while worktreeMode is unset flips that project. The CONFIGURATION.md warning covers this.
